human_tolerance.notes: Breeds in forest; sometimes winters in parks and wooded suburbs (Wikipedia). light_max authored.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: USFS western account: mid-May to late July, peak late May to June. Eastern records run later; not sourced here.

vocalizations.description: Ethereal, flute-like song: a beginning note, then several descending musical phrases in a minor key, repeated at different pitches.
Short call note; its function is not described in the open source used, and its use as an alarm here is a judgement.

external.note: iNaturalist 12890, NCBI 9185, eBird herthr and ITIS 179779 via Wikidata (P3151, P685, P3444, P815).

range.note: Breeding countries CA and US from the Wikipedia distribution sentence; winter range south to Central America is not listed by country, so only CA and US are claimed.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Hop from the shared perching program's ground foraging; Fly from the wings. Gait not verified in an openly licensed source.

traits.nest_type.note: Wikipedia: cup nest on the ground or low in a tree; USFS: usually 0.6-4.6 m up in small trees, occasionally on the ground. Cup chosen as the closest enum value.

traits.perching.note: Perches in trees and shrubs (USFS, Wikipedia description of tree and shrub foraging).

traits.mass_kg.note: 30.1 g in EltonTraits (Dunning08) and in the Scholer dataset mass column.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Derived: -1/ln(0.475) = 1.34 years, rounded to 1.3. Inputs: one adult annual survival estimate (0.475, MAPS mark-recapture, United States, from Desante et al. 2015 as cited in the dataset). Assumes constant annual survival and an adult stage only, so it is an adult-stage mean, not a measured wild lifespan from hatching; first-year mortality is not in the input. Not a maximum longevity.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 80, Diet-Fruit 20 (rounded to 0.8 invertebrate, 0.2 fruit). Wikipedia: mainly insects and berries.

traits.social.note: Authored: solitary outside the breeding season; winter flocks with mixed species not sourced here.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0 supports Diurnal. Wikipedia describes daytime foraging on the forest floor.

traits.defense.note: Authored: flushes to cover (USFS: food searched for seldom far from cover).

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: a woodland thrush that stays near cover; no open wariness measure found.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: shrub thicket cover; USFS notes it is seldom far from cover.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrate weight from diet share; berry weight 0.2 from Diet-Fruit; cup nest sites from USFS and Wikipedia. Berries are not restricted to months: no open monthly source found.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia: breeds in forests, sometimes winters in parks and wooded suburbs. light_max authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: most hermit thrushes migrate south; some remain in northern coastal US and southern Ontario.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding mid-May to late July, peak late May to June, from the USFS western account. Eastern breeding records run to August (Northeast records, not in an open source here), so this window is a western-derived proxy for the US.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Stage list only; no durations sourced.

vocalizations.song.note: Wikipedia: ethereal, flute-like, descending phrases. Time-of-day and season windows are judgement.

vocalizations.call.note: Judgement: the Wikipedia call recording is not described and its function is not stated; the call is used as the alarm by judgement.

look.note: Brown upperparts, reddish tail, white underparts with dark breast spots, pink legs, white eye ring (Wikipedia). Proportions and palette authored.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the species-local program (bt-hermit-thrush-v1); see species/catharus-guttatus/behavior.json.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Judgement, not sourced: Wikipedia says most hermit thrushes migrate south and only some remain in northern coastal US and southern Ontario; no open source gives the resident share. 0.2 is an authored placeholder for review.

sources.note: US federal government work, public domain in the United States. Breeding mid-May to late July, peak late May to June, nests 0.6-4.6 m above ground in small trees, occasionally on the ground, clutch 3-5; food searched for on the ground and forest floor. Account is western/Sierra Nevada-oriented; it is not a national account.
